content:
maria: Heads-up — sketching a tiny proposal to surface per-route sampling + redaction-confidence in the Console. Goal: make debugging real issues easier without increasing PII leakage risk.

sam: high level — do you mean two distinct sample streams (debug vs audit) or a single stream with metadata?

maria: single stream with two tags. debug samples are higher freq but ephemeral (24h TTL, visible in console only). audit samples are extremely rare, archived with stricter access.

devon: For rollout UX: we should default debug_rate low (0.1%?), allow per-route override, and show effective cost impact. Engineers love immediate feedback, but ops must be able to cap.

lisa: how do we compute "redaction-confidence"? model detector score? fuzzy heuristics are noisy — exposing raw score in UI might create false trust.

maria: agreed. plan is to show three things: redaction_mode, confidence_score (0.0-1.0), and a short reason token (e.g., "email", "ssn-like", "attachment-ocr"). Confidence is only used for display and for a console-level filter, not to bypass scrub.

patrick: +1 but warning: embeddings & attachments are big PII sinks. We should not sample attachments by default. If a route accepts file uploads, audit_rate=0, debug_rate=0 unless tenant explicitly opts in.

ops-bot: incident-check: route /v1/ingest-files flagged high sensitivity by policy engine (sensitivity=0.92).

maria: good catch. propose default policy: file routes are opt-in for any sampling. text-only routes get conservative defaults.

sam: can you sketch the JSON config we'd expose in infra? quick example would help product design.

maria: snippet below (proposal):

```yaml
route: /v1/generate
sampling:
  debug_rate: 0.001   # 0.1% visible in Console ephemeral inspect
  audit_rate: 0.00005 # 0.005% to audit store
redaction:
  mode: mask-first   # mask-first | token-hash | remove
  confidence_threshold: 0.85
  attachments: deny_by_default
```

devon: UX note: console should show an inline indicator: "sampling: 0.1% (debug) / 0.005% (audit)" and a small help pop explaining what those samples contain. Add "request->redaction confidence" histogram in route telemetry.

lisa: ops question: when debug samples are viewed in Console, do we require breakglass justification and audit log of who opened it? We need that for compliance customers.

maria: yes — breakglass with justification required; store the justification + actor in audit trail. TTL for debug view = 24h. audit samples stay per retention policy.

patrick: how to handle rollback/rapid disable during incidents? need an immediate kill-switch at org-level to set debug_rate=0 across all routes.

sam: we'll add a global flag and per-tenant override with higher priority. Also show a small banner in Console when any global kill-switch is active.

devon: can we compute expected token cost delta for an org when toggling debug slider? show estimate before they commit.

maria: yes — Console can calculate recent request volume * expected token per request * sampling rate -> cost delta. will add to mock.

lisa: small edgecase: what if redaction_confidence is low but the scrub removed content incorrectly? we need an eval signal to detect regressions.

maria: added: tie these samples into Redwood Optimize evals; run a weekly diff check against gold prompt sets, alert if false-negative scrub rate increases.

patrick: ok by me. next steps?

maria: i'll open a short RFC and a tiny prototype PR for the API + minimal Console UI. assigning initial owner: @devon. please add any compliance caveats.

sam: :thumbsup: thanks — please add a section listing which routes are auto-opt-out (file uploads, embeddings, attachments).

devon: will do. I'll ping infra to wire up the kill-switch and quota cap endpoints.

maria: thanks everyone — will drop RFC link in this thread when done. :eyes:
